_comment: Single source of truth for the 11-week calendar. Transcribed from Curricula/Weeks/week1..11.png; weeks 1, 7 and 11 redistributed for holidays (decisions D-0015..D-0017). Every other path is derived as {week.dir}/{day.slug}. Calendar dates derive from startDate + week index + weekday slot (day 1=Mon..5=Fri); a slot whose date is in holidays is {day, kind: holiday} only. The weekly feedback form is the last teaching day of each week (derived, never hand-set). status flips planned->live when the harness Wire step ships a day. demoFormat: py | nb | none (none = concept day with no code demo; the runbook carries facilitation scripts, D-0030). taught: YYYY-MM-DD, set by the delivery-day close after the session; harness/publish_demos.py copies the answer keys from trainer/<rel>/demos/key/ to demos/<rel>/ only when it is set (D-0030).

weeks.theme: Agile for developers, Git & Python fundamentals
weeks.notes: WEEK ARC (D-0024): Tue = how software teams work (SDLC, Scrum, story pointing, Git as the team's workflow). Wed-Fri = Python the way a team writes it. Audience (D-0048): some programming in any language, no Python, Git, terminal or CS theory assumed, so: Wed assumes the Tue tooling check passed and teaches Python's syntax from first principles (blocks and indentation, variables and types, operators, print and input) together with the conventions a team expects (PEP 8, naming, comments that earn their place); Thu assumes Wed and teaches the data types, then their idioms and pitfalls; Fri assumes Thu and teaches control flow, functions and classes, then when to choose each (when a function, when a class, scope). Every notes page opens by naming in one sentence what it assumes from earlier days of this course and never claims the reader knows anything from outside it.

days.title: Orientation, Agile & Git fundamentals
days.subtitle: SDLC · Scrum · story pointing · git init/commit/branch/merge/push/pull
subtopics: Source control management (git, vcs, cvcs, dvcs)
days.notes: DAY SHAPE (D-0024): the first 30 minutes are an on-ramp, not a lesson: orientation (what/why Python, professionalism at Revature) and a tooling check (interpreter vs compiler, REPL, Jupyter, where Python sits in the full stack) explained briefly from first principles (D-0048: none of it is assumed), enough to confirm the setup works and nothing more. The day's real content is how software teams work: SDLC -> Agile vs waterfall -> Scrum -> story pointing -> Git as the team's workflow -> Git exercise. Notes page: at most ONE step on the on-ramp, every other step on team practice; do not teach Python syntax or pytest (that is Wed-Fri). Demos: at most one on the on-ramp. EXERCISE (D-0025, exerciseKind rubric): the Git exercise IS the exercise: a real repository on GitHub with a feature branch, a merge, one resolved conflict and well-written commit messages, marked against a rubric. No pytest, no starter module.
